chunks: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the deceased making a bequest for the inheritor with something. He said: 'Yes,' or he said: 'It is permissible for him.'

key_terms.الميت: The deceased/dying person — one who is near death or has passed away; here referring to one making a final bequest
key_terms.الوارث: The inheritor/heir — one who receives a share of the estate by right of inheritance (mirath)
key_terms.جائز: Permissible/valid — a legal ruling indicating something is allowed under Islamic law
key_terms.يوصي: To make a bequest (wasiyya) — a testamentary disposition made before death

ai.seo_question: Can a dying person make a bequest to one of their heirs in Islam?
ai.summary: Abu Wallad al-Hannat asked Imam al-Sadiq (AS) whether a dying person may bequeath something to one of his heirs. The Imam affirmed this is permissible, indicating that such a bequest is legally valid despite the general principle that heirs do not inherit through bequest. This ruling addresses a common question in Islamic inheritance law: the deceased's right to make special provision for an inheritor beyond the mandated shares.
